passage:
Subject: Plan check, please

Dear Rehana Ma'am,

I did the calendar from the back this time. The exam is on 14 March, which is 26 weeks away. I took off 5 weeks for revision and 4 weeks for full mock tests, so 17 weeks are left for learning. The syllabus has ten blocks, and by my own speed, they need about two weeks each. That is 20 weeks. So I am three weeks short, and I cannot stretch. I think two blocks with the lowest marks must be cut or shrunk. Would you look at the ten blocks and tell me if you agree which two?

Thank you,
Siddharth

qa.q: How many weeks are left for learning after revision and mocks?
What is Siddharth feeling as the email is written?
qa.a: Siddharth feels a little anxious about being three weeks short, but also practical, since the arithmetic already points to a cut.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Siddharth use to decide which blocks to cut, and why?
qa.a: Siddharth could study past papers to see which blocks carry fewer marks, because counting weeks shows the problem but marks show what is safe to trim.

qa.q: How might Rehana Ma'am see this email?
qa.a: Rehana Ma'am sees a student who has already done the arithmetic and only needs help with the last choice, so Ma'am's advice can be short and targeted.

grounding: Shows working backward from the exam date, subtracting revision and mock periods, and discovering the syllabus does not fit without a cut.

subtype: Approach: working backward from the exam date [Thinking]
passage: Swati, you asked why I dropped two optional topics from my plan. I'll show you the maths. I'm Anjali. On 1 January I counted: the exam is on 24 May. That's twenty weeks. I wanted the last four weeks only for revision, and before that three weeks of full mocks. So twenty minus seven: thirteen weeks for learning the syllabus. Ninety-one days. Then I listed the blocks: polity, history, geography, economy, environment, science, current affairs, and my optional. When I divided, each block got about eleven days. History alone needs twenty, honestly. I sat there feeling a bit sick. The plan didn't fit. So I had to cut. I combined environment with geography, trimmed science to the basics, and dropped two rarely asked optional topics. It hurt. But a plan that doesn't fit isn't a plan. It's a wish.

qa.q: How did Anjali feel on seeing eleven days per block?
qa.a: Anjali felt a bit sick and worried, realising the plan didn't fit and something had to be cut.

qa.q: What else could Anjali do to make the cuts safer?
qa.a: Anjali could check past papers to see which topics are rarely asked, so the cuts fall on low-value areas.

qa.q: How might Swati see Anjali's cuts?
qa.a: Swati, who asked why topics were dropped, gets a clear reason rooted in the dates, which may help Swati check a plan of Swati's own.

grounding: Shows a candidate counting weeks to the exam, subtracting revision and mock periods, and seeing how few days each syllabus block gets, so the plan needs a cut.

subtype: Approach: working backward from the exam date [Thinking]
passage: I'm Devika, Mehak's flatmate, and last Sunday I watched her plan the whole exam year on our kitchen wall. She stuck up a sheet of chart paper and wrote the exam date at the far right: 15 June. Then she counted back the weeks under her breath and wrote "22". She marked the last three weeks in red: "Only revising." The three before that in blue: "Mocks." That left sixteen weeks. She listed her subjects down the side, nine of them, and started dividing. I heard her mutter, "Twelve days for modern history? That's a joke." She stood back for a long time. Then she picked up a pen and crossed out a whole column labelled "Extra reading" and one optional topic. I can't say what she felt; she just said, "Okay. Now it fits," and went to make tea.

qa.q: What date did Mehak write for the exam?
What might Mehak have felt when she muttered about twelve days?
qa.a: Mehak was probably frustrated and worried, seeing that the time left for each subject was too little.

qa.q: What else could Mehak do after cutting?
qa.a: Mehak could check every four weeks whether each block is on time, and adjust before the revision weeks are threatened.

qa.q: How does Devika see the planning?
qa.a: Devika watches closely but only guesses at Mehak's feelings, noticing the long pause before the cuts and the calm now it fits.

grounding: Illustrates a candidate counting back from the exam date, setting aside revision and mock weeks, and cutting the plan once the days per subject look too few.
